extracted.intended_audience: astronomers / mathematicians performing geometric orbital determinations (17th‑century style)
extracted.subtask_short: determine comet orbit from three observations
extracted.subtask_description: A geometric procedure for determining a comet's parabolic (or elliptical) trajectory from three (preferably equally spaced) observations, with practical advice on choosing observations, constructing auxiliary lines and tangents, iterating assumed points, handling observational error, and verifying the derived orbit against additional observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose three observations at (nearly) equal time intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Seligantur tres observationes aequalibus temporum intervallis ab invicem quamproxime distantes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer three observations with equal time intervals. If the comet is moving more slowly, make the middle interval slightly larger so that the difference of times to the sum has the proportion suggested (text gives a practical numeric heuristic: relate to ≈600 days). If such equally spaced observations are not available, obtain a new comet location using lemma VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume a provisional middle location and construct BE toward the Sun
rubrics_metrics.description: In observata longitudine media tB sumatur utcunque punctum B pro loco cometae in plano eclipticae, & inde versus solem ducatur linea BE, quae sit ad sagittam tV, ut contentum sub SB & S t quad. ad cubum hypotenu- sae trianguli rectanguli cujus latera sunt SB & tangens latitudinis cometae in observatione secunda ad radium tB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an assumed point B on the observed middle longitude and construct a specific line BE toward the Sun with the proportions given (uses SB, St, tangents of latitudes and right‑triangle relations). This BE is the starting auxiliary for the geometric construction that yields the approximate first and third observation locations A and C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct line AEC whose parts are proportional to the time intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Per punctum B agatur recta A E C, cujus partes A E, E C, ad rectas TA & TC terminatae, sint ad invicem ut tempora V & W: & erunt A & C loca cometae in plano eclipticae in observatione prima ac tertia quamproxime, si modo B sit locus ejus recte assumptus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw through B a line AEC so that segments AE and EC are in the same ratio as the time intervals between the middle observation and the first and third (V and W). Then A and C approximate the comet's locations at the first and third observations. This step relies on lemma VII and related lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine using perpendiculars, parallels and parallelogram constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad AC bisectam in / erige perpendiculum /t. Per punctum B age occultam Bt ipsi AC parallelam. Junge occultam ^'/ secantem AC in X, & comple parallelogrammum z/Xh-. Cape /o- sequalem 3/X, & per solem kS age occultam a- ^ aequalem sScr-i-^zX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A set sequence of perpendiculars, parallels and parallelogram constructions (as enumerated) produce further auxiliary points used to compute lengths (e.g., MP corresponding to a chord length) and thus to test/adjust the assumed B. Follow the specified geometric operations (lemmas VII–XI) to obtain MP and related segments used later to locate the orbit in its own plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain A and C more accurately by reapplying the same law from a corrected B
rubrics_metrics.description: Et per punctum E iterum duc rectam A E C eadem lege ac prius, id est, ita ut ejus partes A E & E C sint ad invicem ut tempora inter observationes V & W. Et erunt A & C loca cometae magis accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After initial construction, reapply the same proportional construction through the recalculated auxiliary point E to obtain refined A and C. Iteration improves accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tangents to observed latitudes to form further geometric constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad AC bisectam in / erigantur perpendicula A Af, C N, / O, quorum AM & CN sint tangentes latitudinum in observatione prima ac tertia ad radios TA & TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erect perpendiculars at the bisector of AC and take tangents corresponding to observed latitudes at the first and third observations to form lines AM and CN; intersecting these and performing the prescribed constructions yields MN and later MP which measure chord/arclength equivalents for the orbit in its own plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: If MP falls on N then A,B,C give the three true loci in the orbital plane; otherwise extend AC to CG to locate the proper correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Si punctum P incidat in punctum N; erunt A, B, C tria loca cometae, per quae orbis ejus in plano eclipticae describi debet. Sin punctum P non incidat in punctum N; in recta A C capiatur C G ipsi N P sequalis, ita ut puncta (? & P ad easdem partes rectae N C jaceant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the constructed point P coincides with N then the constructed A,B,C are the true comet locations in the ecliptic plane. If not, extend AC and take an appropriate equal segment CG corresponding to NP to obtain the correct correspondence. This handles the mismatch case in the geometric algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate using different assumed B values to produce multiple candidate loci
rubrics_metrics.description: Eadem methodo, qua puncta E, A, C, Gy ex assumpto puncto B inventa sunt, inveniantur ex assumptis utcunque punctis aliis d & ^ puncta nova e, a, c, g, & e, a, k, y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat the construction from other arbitrarily chosen assumed points to generate different candidate loci (sets of A,C etc.). Use intersections or circular constructions through these sets (see below) to determine the comet's locus in the orbital plane more robustly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get the orbital locus by circle intersections and tangents; there may be two possible orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Deinde si per G, g, y ducatur circumferentia circuli Ggy, secans rectam rC in Z: erit Z locus cometae in plano eclipticae. & si in A C, ac, a k capiantur AF, af, a(p ipsis CG, cg, ky respective sequales, & per puncta F, f, X ducatur circumferentia circuli Ff^^, secans rectam ^ 7" in X ; erit punctum X alius cometae locus in plano eclipticae. Ad puncta X si Z erigantur tangentes latitudinum cometae ad radios TX & rZ ; & habebuntur loca duo cometae in orbe proprio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By drawing circles through corresponding constructed points one obtains intersections (Z, X) that are possible comet loci in the ecliptic plane; erecting tangents at these gives two possible loci in the comet's own orbital plane — thus the method can produce two candidate orbits (ambiguous solutions) which must be tested/selected by further data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate and prefer observations/instrumentation with highest accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Suntque p, P, Q, R, S^ T, V, Xy loca cometse in observationibus supra descriptis... Hae observationes telescopio septupedali, & micrometro filisque in foco telescopii locatis peractae sunt: quibus instrumentis & positiones fixarum inter se & positiones cometse ad fixas determinavimus... errores minutum unum primum vix superant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use telescopes with micrometers and focal wires to determine comet positions relative to fixed stars; these instruments yield errors scarcely greater than one minute of arc. Prefer the most accurate observations (first and second here) and note that the third observation may have errors up to ~6–7 minutes; account for such estimated observational errors when selecting data and interpreting residuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose assumed points close to the true location to minimize operations and error
rubrics_metrics.description: Caeterum puncta B, b, /3 non quaelibet, sed vero proxima eligere convenit. Nam si distantia B b perexigua obvenerit; postquam inventa sunt puncta E,/& G, g, actse rectse E / 81 6^^ secabunt TA & TC in punctis qusesitis X & Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumed auxiliary points (B, b, β) should be chosen near the true comet locations; small distances between alternate assumed points reduce the number of operations required and improve accuracy. If B and b are very close, the constructed auxiliary lines will directly cut the required rays at the sought points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate the derived orbit by computing predicted positions and comparing with observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tandem, ut constaret an cometa in orbe sic invento vere moveretur, coegi per operationes partim arithmeticas partim graphicas loca cometae in hoc orbe ad observationum quarundam tempora: uti in tabula sequente videre licet... Observationes cometae hujus a principio ad finem non minus congruunt cum motu cometae in orbe jam descripto, quam motus planetarum congruere solent cum eorum theoriis, & congruendo probant unum & eundem fuisse cometam, qui toto hoc tempore apparuit, ejusque orbem hic recte definitum fuisse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After determining the orbit, compute the comet's positions at the observation times (using arithmetic or graphical computations) and compare to observed longitudes/latitudes. Small residuals and overall congruence with observations are taken as proof the derived orbit is correct. If discrepancies persist, iterate or re-examine observations/assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute orbital elements (nodes, inclination, perihelion, latus rectum, area law) from the constructed orbit
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex quibus orbem definiendo, inveni nodos ejus descendentem in- ss & ascendentem in y^ i^' 53'; inclinationem plani ejus ad planum eclipticae ^i^""- 20'^; verticem ejus distare a nodo ... & esse in^^^^"- 43' cum latitudine australi y^' 34'; & ejus latus rectum esse 236,8, areamque radio ad solem ducto singulis diebus descriptam 93585, quadrato semidiametri orbis magni posito 100000000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the geometrically determined orbit compute classical parameters: ascending/descending nodes, inclination to the ecliptic, argument/longitude of perihelion, latitude at perihelion, latus rectum, area swept per day, semidiameter of the 'great orbit' scale, etc., using scale diagrams and chord/sine tables. These numerical elements allow precise prediction of positions and characterization of the orbit's shape (parabolic vs elliptical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative orbital shapes (parabolic vs elliptical) and test by historic appearances / long‑period fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Porro Halleins observando quod cometa insignis intervallo annorum 575 quater apparuisset ... quaesivit orbem ellipticum cujus axis major esset partium 1382957 ... in quo orbe utique cometa annis 575 revolvi possit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a single orbit type a priori: test both parabolic and elliptical hypotheses. Compare computed orbital period/geometry with historical records of similar apparitions (periodicity) and see which hypothesis yields consistent long‑term fits. Use arithmetic calculations (as Halley did) for more accurate determination of elliptical solutions and periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer arithmetic calculation for highest accuracy; graphical constructions are useful but less precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Postea vero Halleins noster orbitem per calculum arithmeticum accuratlius determinavit, quam per descriptiones linearum fieri licuit; & retinult quidem locum nodorum ... Et ex his datis, calculo eiusdem arithmeticco accurate instituto, loca cometse ad observationum tempora computavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the geometric/graphical construction yields the orbit and is valuable for visualization and initial determination, arithmetic (analytical/numerical) computation delivers higher accuracy; use arithmetic refinement after the geometric construction to get more precise orbital elements and predicted positions.
